conventions: Also tag 'duolingo' if the sentence comes from Duolingo.
Never put the sound tag in Front too: the templates already play Audio with the Latin side.
Set audio.text to the plain Latin text so speech is never generated from HTML.
Voice is eSpeak on purpose: Google's 'la' is not Latin.

fields.Word: Spanish word, nouns with article (la cumbre); expressions as-is
fields.WordType: one of N, V, Adj, Adv, Expr, Prep, Pron, Conj, Num
fields.Gender: m, f or m/f for nouns; empty otherwise

conventions: Leave Word_suffix, Word_hint, Meaning_suffix, Meaning_hint empty.
Tag Spanish::Duolingo::<nn>_<Topic> if the user names a matching topic, otherwise Spanish::Added.

fields.Word: French word, nouns with article (le copain); expressions as-is
fields.WordType: one of N, NPl, V, Adj, Adv, Expr, Prep, Pron, Conj, Num
fields.Gender: m, f or m/f for nouns; empty otherwise

conventions: Leave Word_suffix, Word_hint, Meaning_suffix, Meaning_hint empty.
Tag French::Duolingo::<nn>_<Topic> if the user names a matching topic, otherwise French::Added.

fields.Text: (part of speech) definition. Example sentence with the word as {{c1::word}}; an optional IPA transcription may follow the word inside the cloze, e.g. {{c1::virile /ˈvɪr.əl/}}

conventions: Audio speaks only the cloze word: use add_audio with cloze_only=true (IPA and hints are dropped).
For new notes via add_notes, set audio.text to the plain cloze word without transcription.

Google en-US (and en-CA) mispronounces some rare words, e.g. chimerical; en-GB got it right. If the user reports a wrong pronunciation, they clear Back Extra in Anki and you re-voice that one note with en-GB; if en-GB is wrong too, try macos:Samantha (used for kvetch).
